title: Coming soon on ZDF: Mission Pinguin
text:
Carsten Behrendt, who joined the expedition, during the editing of the documentary.
From the Drake Passage to the penguin colonies of the Danger Islands, a new ZDF documentary brings our Antarctic expedition to the screen.
In Mission Pinguin – Mit dem Segelboot in die Antarktis, reporter Carsten Behrendt follows the scientists and sailors aboard Malizia Explorer, with Boris Herrmann. The approximately 43-minute film offers an insight into Antarctic field research, wildlife, and the challenges of reaching these remote islands.

title: Danger Islands: Esther Horvath’s exhibition in Zingst
text:
Esther Horvath’s exhibition Danger Islands brings Antarctic field research to Germany’s Baltic coast. Opened on 29 May 2026 as part of the horizonte zingst environmental photography festival, it is on view at Schlösschen Sundische Wiese in Zingst until 7 November 2026.
In December 2025, Esther joined Boris Herrmann aboard Malizia Explorer to document a scientific expedition to the Danger Islands. The remote archipelago is home to an immense population of breeding Adélie penguins. Thick pack ice and harsh weather made access difficult; ultimately, the team had just 12 hours on land to carry out its work.
Through her photographs, Esther offers a rare view of the people and research behind the expedition—and the challenges of working in one of Antarctica’s least accessible places.

title: Danger Islands: Esther Horvath’s exhibition in Zingst
text:
A conversation beyond the photographs
On 31 May 2026, a Horizonte Talk at the Multimediahalle Zingst brought scientists from the expedition team together for a panel discussion. They shared insights into their research, the realities of Antarctic fieldwork, and why these findings matter for understanding a changing planet.

title: Behind the scenes of polar science with Esther Horvath
section: A journey into the world behind the photographs
text:
A journey into the world behind the photographs
In December 2025, Esther Horvath joined professional sailor Boris Herrmann aboard Malizia Explorer for the Danger Islands expedition in Antarctica. The journey became the cover story of GEO’s August issue.
In her talks on the main stage and Nikon stage at Imaging World, Esther takes audiences behind the scenes of that mission—and into the wider world of polar research.
From the Arctic polar night and expeditions across sea ice to the penguin colonies of the Danger Islands, she shares how scientists work in remote environments and how she documents their research through photography. Alongside the images are the people, challenges, and moments that rarely make it into a finished story.
Her perspective offers a close look at modern polar science and a connection to places whose changes shape our shared future.

title: Our Mission
text:
ANTARCTIC WILDLIFE PROTECTION

Science under sail. Wildlife conservation through knowledge.
Our mission is to build the scientific foundation for protecting Antarctica’s most important wildlife habitats.
Starting in 2027/28, our international team will return every two years to the Antarctic Peninsula and the Danger Islands aboard Malizia Explorer. By tracking penguins and other seabirds, monitoring their colonies, and uncovering past ecosystem change, we will identify the places these animals depend on—and build the long-term evidence needed to guide their protection.

title: Become a Partner
text:
Adélie penguins on the ice with Malizia Explorer anchored nearby.




SCIENCE · SAILING · SHARED PURPOSE


Partnerships help make our research possible—from reaching remote Antarctic habitats to sharing what we discover.
We welcome conversations with individuals, foundations, companies, and organisations who would like to contribute. Support can take many forms: funding, equipment, practical expertise, or helping our findings reach new audiences.
Start a conversation

title: Become a Partner
section: Different ways to make a difference
text:
Different ways to make a difference
There is no single way to become involved. Together, we can explore where your interests and our research needs meet.


Expeditions & fieldwork
Help make research voyages possible through support for transport, expedition logistics, and the time needed to work in remote Antarctic habitats.


Scientific equipment & research
Contribute towards tracking devices, field instruments, laboratory analyses, or tools that help us understand wildlife and its habitats.


Knowledge & practical expertise
Bring skills, services, or technical support—from equipment development and field logistics to data analysis and interpretation.


Education & communication
Help bring Antarctic research into classrooms and share its discoveries through photography, films, exhibitions, and public engagement.

title: Become a Partner
text:
Small devices. A wider understanding.
Tracking devices help reveal where penguins and other seabirds find food—and which marine habitats they depend on.
Supporting equipment is one practical way to contribute to this work. Combined with repeated field observations and colony monitoring, these measurements help build the evidence needed to guide habitat protection.

title: The Team
text:
Simeon Lisovski
Scientific Lead · Polar Ecology & Conservation
Simeon is a researcher at the Alfred Wegener Institute and the Leibnitz Insitute for Zoo and Wildlife Research specialising in polar biology and seabird ecology. He studies how environmental change affects wildlife, animal movements, and ecosystem health, with Antarctic fieldwork on Adélie penguins, skuas, and southern giant petrels. His research also examines how pathogens reach Antarctica and how avian influenza circulates among seabirds. For Antarctic Wildlife Protection, he leads the scientific programme, linking seabird tracking and colony monitoring to habitat conservation.
Meet Simeon at AWI ↗

title: The Team
text:
Esther Horvath
Photography & Science Communication
Esther is a documentary and science photographer whose work brings polar research and the people behind it into public view. Since 2015, she has documented scientific expeditions in the polar regions, including the MOSAiC expedition. Her photography received a World Press Photo award in 2020. Through photographs and stories, she connects audiences with Antarctic wildlife, the realities of field research, and the importance of protecting these environments.
Website ↗ · Instagram ↗

title: The Team
text:
Team Malizia
Research Platform, Outreach & Ocean Education
Boris Herrmann and his Team Malizia connects offshore sailing with ocean science, education, and climate action. The team contributes the research sailing vessel Malizia Explorer, alongside its communication and education activities. Its My Ocean Challenge programme brings ocean and climate science to young people—including live connections between classrooms and Antarctic expeditions. Together, these contributions help researchers reach remote habitats and bring the expedition’s discoveries to audiences beyond the scientific community.
Discover Malizia Explorer ↗

title: Modern polar explorers: Esther Horvath at the Royal Geographical Society
text: On 6 August 2026, polar photographer and National Geographic Explorer Esther Horvath spoke at the Royal Geographical Society in London, marking the 125th anniversary of the Discovery Expedition. Her talk included photographs and experiences from the Danger Islands expedition aboard Malizia Explorer.

title: Modern polar explorers: Esther Horvath at the Royal Geographical Society
text:
A different kind of discovery
Polar regions have always been places where knowledge is hard-won. Historic expeditions travelled into largely unknown landscapes. Today, Esther documents a different kind of exploration: the work of scientists investigating how ice, oceans, atmosphere, and ecosystems are changing.
Their discoveries are new insights into a transforming planet. Through her photography, Esther shows how researchers collect data in extreme cold, work through polar darkness, and build the long-term observations that underpin our understanding of climate and environmental change.
Her work brings these experiences beyond the field—making visible both the changes unfolding in the Arctic and Antarctic and the people dedicated to understanding them.

title: Education
text:
TOGETHER WITH TEAM MALIZIA’S MY OCEAN CHALLENGE


What can a penguin tell us about the ocean? How do scientists work among sea ice and storms? And why does Antarctica matter to all of us?
Together with My Ocean Challenge, we want to turn questions like these into opportunities to learn. We connect Antarctic field research with the curiosity of young people—through conversations, photographs, and stories from the expedition.
Discover My Ocean Challenge ↗






Pupils gathered for a live connection with the Antarctic expedition team. Photo: Stefan Junker.

title: Education
section: Learning together with My Ocean Challenge
text:
Learning together with My Ocean Challenge
My Ocean Challenge is Team Malizia’s education programme, connecting sailing with ocean and climate learning. Our collaboration builds on that work, bringing Antarctic wildlife, polar research, and first-hand expedition experience into the conversation.
We are developing ways to contribute additional classroom talks, learning materials, and encounters with the people behind the science. We want these activities to complement My Ocean Challenge and give teachers practical ways to explore Antarctic ecosystems with their pupils.

title: Education
text:
What we are working towards


01

Meet the expedition team
Classroom talks and opportunities to ask researchers, sailors, and photographers about their work, wildlife, and life on an Antarctic expedition.



02

Explore the science
Learning materials that connect penguins, food webs, tracking, and environmental change with the questions our team investigates in the field.



03

Follow the discoveries
Photographs and expedition stories that help make remote places tangible and encourage young people to ask their own questions about ocean protection.



Activities and new materials are being developed together. Please contact us to discuss interests and availability.

title: Education
text:
Classroom in the ice
During the 2025 Antarctic expedition, around 120 pupils in Kiel joined the team virtually aboard Malizia Explorer for an hour. Scientists, sailors, and photographers answered their questions as the vessel travelled through Antarctic waters towards the Danger Islands.
The exchange brought expedition life into the classroom—and pupils’ curiosity directly to the people doing the research. It is a starting point for the educational work we want to continue together.
Read the story on Team Malizia ↗
